entry.title: HypeScore
entry.summary: A real-time hype meter that watches your webcam and scores your energy. Dance, move, or just vibe — it reads your motion and gives you a hype score you can actually see.
entry.content:
HypeScore — Turn Your Energy Into a Number

URL: https://hypescore.jasonwang.us
Stack: React, MediaPipe pose detection, WebAssembly, Web Workers

What It Is

HypeScore is a real-time hype meter. You turn on your webcam, move around, and it gives you a score based on your energy and movement.

It’s not a fitness tracker. It’s not counting steps or calories. It’s measuring hype — how much energy you’re putting into the moment.

What It Does

  • Reads your movement through your webcam using pose detection and optical flow
  • Scores your energy in real time with a live hype gauge
  • Shows signal analysis — rhythm, energy, and density telemetry as you move
  • Switches between FFT and CWT signal engines for different analysis styles
  • Has a Zen mode with six visual styles that react to your movement
  • Works with video files too — upload a recording and score it retroactively

How It Works

You open the page, grant camera access, and start moving. The app processes your webcam feed through MediaPipe pose detection and optical flow to measure motion. A signal engine (your choice of FFT or Continuous Wavelet Transform) turns that motion into a live hype score.

The score updates every frame. Dance, jump, gesture, or just wave your arms — watch the number go up.

When you want to zone out, hit Zen mode and pick from six visual styles that pulse and shift with your energy.

Tech Stack

Layer Technology
Frontend React + Vite
Pose detection MediaPipe
Signal analysis FFT & CWT, Web Workers
Styling Tailwind CSS
Hosting Static files via nginx

entry.title: Possible Nodes
entry.summary: Map out your next big decision and watch how each choice ripples forward — before you commit to anything.
entry.content:
See the Future Before You Step Into It

URL: https://future.jasonwang.us
Stack: Python FastAPI

What It Is

You’re about to make a decision. Maybe it’s a job change. Maybe it’s moving cities. Maybe it’s something smaller but still important. You can guess what happens next. Or you can see it. This is a system for modeling causal relationships and exploring “what if” scenarios before you commit.

What It Does

  • Map out your options — lay out each choice and see what branches from it
  • Follow each path — the system shows likely outcomes, dead ends, and unexpected connections
  • Simulate decisions — it’s like a flight simulator for your life choices
  • Stop hoping — see where each path leads before you take the first step

How It Works

You build a directed acyclic graph of your decisions — each node is a choice or event, each edge is a causal link. You pick a starting point and follow the graph forward. The system shows you what happens downstream from each choice, so you can compare paths before committing to any one of them.

Tech Stack

Layer Technology
Backend Python FastAPI
Graph model Custom DAG implementation
Reverse proxy nginx
Process manager PM2

entry.title: NicheApp
entry.summary: Every paper you read, every connection you make, every insight — saved, connected, and actually findable six months from now.
entry.content:
Stop Losing Research Papers in Your Browser Tabs

URL: https://niche.jasonwang.us
Stack: Python FastAPI, SQLite, wiki-style frontend

What It Is

You know the feeling. You find a great paper, read half of it, tell yourself you’ll come back, and then it’s buried under twenty other tabs. Three months later you remember there was something useful in there, but you can’t find it. This is your research memory — every paper you read, every connection you make, every insight — saved, connected, and actually findable six months from now.

What It Does

  • Save papers as you read them — arXiv, bioRxiv, anything you’re studying
  • Highlight what matters — mark the insights that actually matter to you
  • Connect papers — link Paper A to Paper B when you notice they’re talking about the same thing
  • Search your memory — six months from now, search for “causal inference” or “protein folding” and every relevant paper you’ve ever read shows up, with your notes still attached
  • Daily auto-ingest — new papers pulled automatically every morning

How It Works

You save papers as you encounter them. The system ingests new papers daily from arXiv and bioRxiv. You add your own notes and connections between papers. When you need to find something later, it’s all there — not scattered across browser tabs, but organized and searchable.

entry.title: Zhuyin Trainer
entry.summary: Stop sounding like a foreigner. Learn Mandarin using Zhuyin — the phonetic system Taiwan uses — so you actually pronounce tones and sounds correctly from day one.
entry.content:
Finally Learn Mandarin Pronunciation Without Pinyin Confusion

URL: https://zhuyin.jasonwang.us
Stack: Node.js, Next.js, vanilla JavaScript

What It Is

Pinyin lies to you. It uses familiar English letters, so your brain reads them like English. “q” isn’t “q.” “x” isn’t “x.” You think you’re saying it right, and native speakers hear something completely different. This trainer uses Zhuyin (Bopomofo) — the phonetic system Taiwan actually uses to teach kids — so you learn the sounds exactly as they are, with no bad habits.

What It Does

  • Learn Zhuyin symbols — a complete set of phonetic characters that don’t pretend to be English
  • Hear the sounds — audio for every symbol so you know exactly how to pronounce it
  • Practice until it sticks — drill until your mouth knows what to do
  • Reader mode — see Zhuyin layered over real Mandarin text and read it out loud

How It Works

You start with the symbols, hear how each one sounds, and practice until you can read Mandarin text with Zhuyin annotations. No false cognates, no English letter tricks — just the sounds, exactly as they are.

entry.title: VTOL Drone Simulator
entry.summary: Fly a VTOL drone in real time and watch every control decision play out before your eyes. No black boxes, no mystery — just you, the sticks, and the physics.
entry.content:
Stop Guessing Your Drone Flights — See Exactly What’s Happening in Real Time

URL: https://drone.jasonwang.us
Stack: React, Three.js, Rapier physics, Zustand

What It Is

This is a VTOL drone flight simulator that runs in your browser. You’re not watching a video — you’re flying a simulated drone and seeing every control decision happen in real time. Every tilt, every correction, every control surface moving as you manipulate the sticks.

What It Does

  • Fly a VTOL drone — take off, hover, maneuver, and land in a 3D environment
  • Choose your flight style — smooth and steady, aggressive and responsive, or adaptive to changing conditions
  • See every control decision — watch control surfaces move and the drone respond stick by stick
  • No black-box autopilot — you choose the controller, you see what it does, you learn what actually works

How It Works

You open the simulator in your browser and start flying. The physics engine (Rapier) handles gravity, thrust, and aerodynamics in real time. You pick a controller — PID, LQR, MPC, SMC, or Adaptive — and each one responds differently to your inputs. The 3D scene renders with Three.js so you can see the drone from every angle as you fly.

No installation, no setup. Just open it and fly.

Tech Stack

Layer Technology

Build tool Vite
3D rendering Three.js + @react-three/fiber
Physics @react-three/rapier

entry.content:
Every city has a secret language—a hidden history etched into its architecture and a vibrant energy pulse in its local events. Often, as travelers, we only scratch the surface. This realization was the spark for my latest experiment: a personal, AI-powered companion designed to unveil the hidden stories of the world in real-time.

I’m excited to share the journey of creating an AI-assisted tour guide app that transforms a simple walk into an immersive exploration.

The Vision: More than a Map

The goal wasn’t just to list landmarks, but to synthesize a rich, interactive, and personalized touring experience using the power of Large Language Models (LLMs).

What it does:

  • Intelligent Landmark Discovery: The app doesn’t just look for markers; it understands the context of your surroundings to suggest meaningful points of interest.
  • Narrative Weaving: By researching local events and deep history, it provides more than just facts—it tells the story of the place.
  • Multi-Sensory Interaction: Every discovery includes a guided introduction, a visual context, and seamless audio narration to keep your eyes on the world, not your screen.

Experience the experiment for yourself here:

Explore the AI Tour Guide

New Link

This is just the beginning of how we can use AI to deepen our connection with the physical world. I’m eager to hear how it changes your perspective on your next journey.
